These synthetic stores contain no real board data.

`legacy-complete.sqlite`, `legacy-reopened.sqlite`, and `collision.sqlite` are
the retained X2 fixtures created through the shipped `BoardStore` at Router
`ffced1c1c3c84e0ca41701fb9eb4326acea2451e`. Their source and oracle are preserved
with the local design experiment `x2-import-fidelity-report.md`.

`role-history.sqlite` is generated by the adjacent `fixture-builder`, pinned to
that same Router commit. It covers a role rejoin without a leave or post, a
handover promoting an already-open participant, a human creator with no stored
role attribution, and an empty topic with a description.

Regenerate from the repository root (use the normal workspace build target):

```sh
CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo run --manifest-path crates/board-legacy-upgrade/tests/fixture-builder/Cargo.toml --target-dir target -- crates/board-legacy-upgrade/tests/fixtures/role-history.sqlite
```

The generator refuses to overwrite an existing fixture. Its dependency is pinned
to the shipped legacy commit, and its Cargo.lock is retained.

`watch-scope.sqlite` adds a topic-only watch followed by a reply in a thread with
no explicit thread watch. `mixed-watch-scope.sqlite` combines a topic watch with
an explicit watch on one thread and replies in both watched and unwatched
threads. Both are generated by the same pinned public API builder, using its
`watch-scope` and `mixed-watch-scope` arguments respectively. The shipped inbox
predicate is the oracle; topic watches do not enter its reply selection.

The reader's `src/legacy_schema_identity.json` records the normalized
`sqlite_master` definitions (including `_sqlx_migrations`) and the eight applied
migration identities from `role-history.sqlite`. Migration checksums were also
checked against SHA-384 of the eight SQL files at the pinned source commit.
Only SQL whitespace is normalized, as in the shipped schema validator. The
importer compares this metadata read-only; it never executes those definitions
or applies missing migrations. `source_schema_refusals.rs` mutates disposable
copies to prove changed schema, missing tracking, altered migration history and
extra checkpoint rows fail before board-data decoding without changing bytes or
modification time.

`project_description.rs` and the CLI refusal case alter disposable copies of
`role-history.sqlite`, retaining the shipped schema and migration metadata.
They arrange empty, multiline/control and exactly 16,384-byte Unicode/control
descriptions for exact native `ProjectState` readback. An over-bound value
must produce a topic-named typed refusal and leave source bytes unchanged.
